text: alice: heads-up — noticed slow but steady memory climb on the qwen long-context canaries since last night. ~120MB/hr on one pod. correlates with rope_scale >= 8192 and mixed GQA/MQA runs. logs attached./n/nben: can you paste the minimal repro command? can try to repro locally./n/nalice: here is what I used:/n```/n./bench_longctx --model=qwen-14k --seq=32000 --clients=8 --batch=auto --rope-scale=8192 --profile-heap /tmp/heap.pbz/ndefaults: batch_window_ms=12/ndefaults: prefetch_pages=2/ndefaults: slab_threshold=256/ndefaults: kernel_selector=auto/ndef```/npprof snapshot shows:/n```/nKVPage.alloc_count: 245000/nKVPage.evictions: 32000/nheap_grow_rate: 120MB/h/npage_churn_rate: 4200/min/nevict_reclaim_lag: 4.1s/ndefault_kernel: matmul_avx_fallback (switched at seq>4096)/n```/n/ndana: interesting — fallback kernel switch + rope crossing could fragment slab metadata. MQA vs GQA may change token grouping which breaks page coalescing. also we have deep batching hysteresis (batch_window_ms=12) which keeps more active pages around while trying to batch, increasing residency./n/nbob: (cc @charlie) do we have a recent change to allocator coalesce? I thought we tuned slab_threshold down in last month./n/ncharlie: we did reduce coalesce aggressiveness for <512 pages to reduce stall spikes, might be related. quick theory:/n- when kernel_selector flips to fallback implementation we emit more, smaller KV writes (smaller page footprints) which defeats the slab coalescer and increases fragmentation./n- rope scaling passing >8192 increases KV slot aliases leading to prefetched pages touching different slabs, preventing reuse./n/nben: can you try a quick mitigation? suggestions:/n- bump slab_threshold 256->512/n- reduce batch_window_ms 12->6/n- enable prefix_cache for this model (prefetch_pages=4) to consolidate accesses/n/nalice: ran the three locally on the canary (one pod) — results below:/n```/nconfig: slab_threshold=512, batch_window_ms=6, prefetch_pages=4/ngrowth_rate: 15MB/h (was 120MB/h)/npage_churn_rate: 600/min (was 4200/min)/nevict_reclaim_lag: 0.9s (was 4.1s)/nheap_peak: reduced by ~1.6GB/ndefault_kernel still flips but less churn observed/ndef```/n/alice: this looks promising as a short-term mitigation. /n/dana: nice, that suggests fragmentation pressure is sensitive to those params. we should be cautious about reduced batch_window impact on token-ops cost though. need perf numbers for latency and throughput tradeoffs./n/ben: I'll run a small A/B across 4 pods for 2 hours with traffic replay. will collect token-ops, p50/p95 latency, and unit-cost change. /n/charlie: longer term: we should add a kernel_selector override rule: if model.name matches qwen-* and rope_scale>=4096 and seq >= 8192 then prefer kernel_v2_coalesce (the one that outputs larger contiguous KV writes). also consider re-enabling coalesce for <512 pages but with background low-priority compaction to avoid stalls./n/dana: +1 and add an eval that stresses mixed GQA/MQA batching patterns — they diverge significantly in write grouping. create an alert tied to page_churn_rate > 2000/min and heap_growth > 50MB/h (5m) for canaries./n/deploy-bot: deploy plan created: rollout=canary(4 pods)->30m metrics gate->if page_churn_rate drops by >=60% and p95 latency change <=+5% then promote. Change set: slab_threshold=512, batch_window_ms=6, prefetch_pages=4, add kernel_selector override for qwen longctx./n/ben: kicked off replay + metrics. will post results in ~40m. /n/alice: awesome, thanks. if we verify this we'll include a regression test in perf-harness that replays mixed GQA/MQA sequences to avoid a future reversion. /n/charlie: filing follow-ups: 1) allocator coalesce re-eval PR, 2) kernel selector rule PR, 3) perf-harness repro. /n/dana: filing alert rule + dashboard panel for KV churn. /n/ben: preliminary results after 45m:/n- churn down 68%/n- heap_growth now flat (within noise)/n- p50 latency +2%, p95 +4% (acceptable per SLO)/n/charlie: perfect. let's hold the canary for 2 hours and then roll to the rest of the cluster. also need to run same test on Mistral/llama to check cross-model differences. Qwen looked worst-case here but might mask MQA-specific regressions elsewhere./n/alice: noted — I'll queue Mistral/llama runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
